gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-arimo: Cultural through and through, Edo SZ draws its letters like fine rope, with cast-iron stature in the lowercase. Arimo does its best work quietly: a sans-serif with a tall mean line and spacious gaps where curves end.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-biryani: Cast-iron stature up top, friendly openness below. What carries it is consistency: Edo SZ keeps one stroke width throughout, and Biryani, a sans with large open eyes on every e, never clogs.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-carrois-gothic: Cut cord letters, stood up tall. Edo SZ lays rounded, constant strokes beside Carrois Gothic, a sans-serif with generous c openings and a high x-height, so classic craft meets a modern, orderly neighbor.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Edo SZ moves with a marker-nib line that ignores direction, its lowercase standing like cast iron capitals. And Carrois Gothic SC, a sans whose capitals and lowercase nearly match in height, makes consistency the pair's real strength.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-chivo: Edo SZ bends thin steel rod into every letter. Its strength is stature and constancy, while Chivo, a sans with lowercase packed up toward the caps, is built for visible daylight in every curve.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-duru-sans: Duru Sans reads clean and modern, its small-letter bodies dominating while ascenders hardly show. And Edo SZ, drawn like cable with every stroke holding one thickness, makes the pair feel like old craft beside modern ease.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-funnel-sans: Funnel Sans reads clean and professional, its strokes holding steady from stem to curve and its e opened like a pried clasp. And Edo SZ brings cast-iron stature in a lowercase of one constant stroke width.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-georama: Edo SZ draws its curves with no pinching at all. Georama brings plain sans curves too, its c pulled apart like a bracelet, so unpinched smoothness is what this pair does best.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-gidole: Gidole reads clean, its terminals parted like open scissor blades and a neon-tube consistency in every stroke. And Edo SZ brings cast-iron stature to the lowercase where Gidole, in plain sans, brings quiet clarity.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-hedvig-letters-sans: Approachable from the first line, Hedvig Letters Sans leaves a wide gap where the c ends, its small letters nearly capital height. Under Edo SZ, with curves and straights sharing one width, pages read smoothly.
